clue.text: Obsequious warrant-officer and his military force

parts.note: a sergeant major, abbreviated SM, holds a warrant officer's rank in the British Army
an army is a land military force

explanation.surface: A fawning sergeant major and the troops under him.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes an oily, ingratiating manner, a close synonym of obsequious.

clue.text: Kentish girl shown round popular college

parts.note: Kent is in south-east England, abbreviated SE

indicators.note: the girl's name is displayed wrapped around the word for popular, so it goes inside her

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A girl from Kent is given a tour of a well-liked college.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent lies in the south-east corner of England, which gives the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college, especially one training priests.

clue.text: Stevenson, lacking a book, improvised

indicators.note: lacking says the name is short of the letter for the clue's a

parts.note: Adlai Stevenson was the US Democratic presidential candidate of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A politician, missing a script, spoke off the cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad lib is to speak or perform without preparation, so improvised.

clue.text: Queen's sound accommodation for hawks

definitions.meaning: a queen is a female cat
a cage or shed where hawks are kept while moulting

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a cat's cry and a falconer's cage for moulting hawks.

clue.text: Fool taken in by a rugby player's left-wing hype

indicators.note: the fool is received inside the following words, so it sits within them

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum
git is British slang for a stupid person

explanation.surface: A forward's idiot friend spreads socialist propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union a prop is one of the two forwards either side of the hooker in the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political, originally communist, propaganda, hence left-wing hype.

clue.text: Dress binding made by everyone in Eccles, for example

indicators.note: in says the word for everyone sits inside the comic character

parts.note: Eccles was a character in The Goon Show, a British radio comedy, so he is a Goon
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Trimming for a gown made by all the people of a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles looks like the town near Manchester; it is the Goon Show character.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloon is a narrow braid or lace used to trim or bind the edges of clothing.

clue.text: Game merry king included among successes

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, merry

indicators.note: the king's letter is placed amid the word for successes

parts.note: wins are successes
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tipsy monarch joins a run of victories in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a game of flicking small discs into a cup.

clue.text: About gold missing from bridal outfit — it's turned up!

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: missing from says the symbol for gold is absent from the outfit word

parts.note: a trousseau is the clothes a bride collects for her marriage
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A bride's gold-free wedding outfit has finally shown up.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé describes a nose that is turned up at the tip.

clue.text: Traveller climbing with young relative? He's the third

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller or salesman
a son is a young relative

explanation.surface: A salesman goes up the mountain with his boy, who makes three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is grammatically the third person, the sense the clue's last words give.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'he' belongs to the third person, so the clue names one example of a grammatical category.

clue.text: Potter's craft?

parts.note: a potter makes pots and jugs, and a craft is also a ship, so the phrase reads both ways

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a container a potter makes and a ship, a craft on water.

clue.text: Revolutionary device channelling power for the daily grind?

definitions.text: Revolutionary device channelling power for the daily grind?

parts.words: Revolutionary device channelling power for the daily grind?
parts.note: a turning wheel driven by water in a mill race, used to grind corn; revolutionary and grind sound political and drudging

explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turned by water drives the stones that grind grain in a mill.

clue.text: Discourage bloke dropping off cleanser

indicators.note: dropping off says the man's word falls away from the cleanser

parts.note: detergent is a cleansing agent
gent, short for gentleman, means a man or bloke

explanation.surface: Put off a man falling asleep over the washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' suggests falling asleep; here the man is removed from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting.

clue.text: Pooter's sweet, but not a pushover!

parts.note: Charles Pooter is the narrator of The Diary of a Nobody, the Grossmiths' comic novel, so he is the Nobody
a fool is a dessert of puréed fruit and cream

explanation.surface: A comic diarist's pudding, yet no soft touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Pooter is the self-important clerk who writes The Diary of a Nobody, a classic of English comic fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is nobody's fool is shrewd and cannot easily be taken advantage of.

clue.text: Girl's drawing producing bewilderment

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name, here with its possessive s
traction is the act of drawing or pulling

explanation.surface: A girl's sketch leaves viewers confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraction can mean a state of mental confusion or agitation, close to bewilderment.

clue.text: Triumphant cry when 23 is banished from state

indicators.note: is banished from says the letter is thrown out of the state's name

parts.note: Ohio is a US state
the answer at 23 across is a number, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An exultant shout as someone is exiled from the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oho is an exclamation of triumph or surprised discovery.

clue.text: Denial from judge meeting American gangster

parts.note: a referee, ref, judges a game
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A judge sits down with a US mobster and turns him down.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a denial of a request.

clue.text: Ham, possibly, drinking in Leah's tangled story

indicators.note: drinking means the food takes in the scrambled letters, as if swallowing them

parts.note: ham is one example of food

indicators.note: tangled means the letters of the name are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Ham soaking up drink in a woman's messy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' wants to be an over-the-top actor; it is just one kind of food. 'tangled' makes ALSEH, which 'drinking' takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untrue story, a lie.

clue.text: Not at all negative, like Solomon

parts.note: no is a negative reply
King Solomon is proverbial for his wisdom

explanation.surface: Far from negative, as wise as a biblical king.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowise is an old adverb meaning in no way, not at all.

clue.text: Traditional pen for animal features ultimately in song

parts.note: a sty is a pen for a pig

indicators.note: in says the final letter is placed within the song word

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of features

explanation.surface: A pig's pen appears at the end of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Lied (plural Lieder) is the German word for a song, borrowed in English for art songs by Schubert and others.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylised means following a conventional, formal style rather than being naturalistic.

clue.text: Girl in service?

definitions.meaning: a hymn of praise sung in the Mass, a church service

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a woman's name and a hymn sung in church services.

clue.text: A heartless critic, one exploiting Zola, for example

indicators.note: heartless means the inside of critic is removed, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: a user is someone who exploits others

explanation.surface: A critic with no feelings takes advantage of a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola's open letter J'accuse ('I accuse') denounced the French army in the Dreyfus affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola publicly accused the authorities of injustice, making him one example of an accuser.

clue.text: Touching article by leader of group in shelter

indicators.note: in says the article and the group's first letter go inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: leader of points to the first letter of group

explanation.surface: Moving words from the head of a group in a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent line just touches a curve; the word comes from Latin for touching.

clue.text: Film story about Mozart's first composition

indicators.note: about says the story wraps around the catalogue number

parts.note: a tale is a story
Mozart's works are numbered in the Köchel catalogue, K; his first is K1, with I as the Roman one

explanation.surface: An account of the first piece Mozart ever wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie is an early film with a soundtrack.

clue.text: Bad luck some people bring? Which ones, say?

indicators.note: say means the question is spoken, giving what it sounds like

parts.note: the reply to 'some people bring bad luck' asking which ones is 'Who do?'

explanation.surface: Some people bring misfortune, but which?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a little exchange: someone says some people bring bad luck, and the questioner asks 'Who do?', which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx, something or someone that brings bad luck.

clue.text: Cardinal achieved mastery in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: won means gained victory or mastery

explanation.surface: A churchman prevailed through his oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman; here it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, of which this is the first.

clue.text: Contract a woman will put together, securing small boat

parts.note: to cockle is to pucker or wrinkle, contracting into folds
she'll is short for she will, a woman will

explanation.surface: An agreement a woman will assemble to secure a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like an agreement; it is a verb, to pucker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockleshell is a small, light boat, likened to the shell of a cockle.

clue.text: Incident involving priest in film

indicators.note: involving says the film's title wraps around the priest's title

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial
Ven., the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A scene featuring a cleric in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Archdeacons in the Church of England are styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an incident, something that happens.

clue.text: Police officer seizing stolen garment in India

indicators.note: seizing says the officer's letters hold the word for stolen

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A detective grabs stolen clothing in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India.

clue.text: Lacking initiative, with no time to work?

parts.note: a shift is a period of working time
with no X can be written X-less

explanation.surface: Someone with no get-up-and-go and no job to clock in for.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftless means lazy and lacking ambition or resourcefulness.

clue.text: Bond's equality of attainment

definitions.meaning: a result where both sides finish level

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a binding link and a level result in a contest.

clue.text: Common soldiers given name in journal

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in says the letter for name sits inside the journal word

parts.note: a diary is a journal

explanation.surface: Private soldiers get named in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the British Army term for soldiers below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary means common, usual or unremarkable.

clue.text: Write a little for small group

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: Jot down a bit for a little team.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a set of five, a small group.
